short: Applies an ECoG articulatory-versus-phoneme encoding comparison (Chartier 2018) to sEMG in three speech modes; the gain is small, mode contrasts are confounded, and no decoder is tested.
position: The paper changes the predictor space of a forward sEMG encoding model (M06, SPARC articulatory features against phoneme one-hots) and how silent EMG gets its features (M02, features from paired aloud audio, silent EMG warped to the aloud EMG by DTW); both are standard. The same articulatory-versus-phoneme comparison was made on ECoG with session-held-out tests and the same outcome (Chartier et al. 2018), so the contribution is the signal and the speech modes. The only tabulated effect is small (Gaddy single subject: mean r 0.455 against 0.443 voiced, 0.364 against 0.346 mimed), and the 24-participant results are plotted only. Mode contrasts mix 14 aloud features with 12 silent ones and depend on a DTW warp to the aloud trial that the null leaves in place. No decoder is trained, so the claim about better SSI intermediates is untested; folds, seeds and sessions are unstated.
